research.approach: Social managers facing falling engagement first check the measure, then the posting habits, then the content. They confirm how engagement rate is calculated and compare like with like, because rates by followers and rates by reach differ a lot and follower growth lowers a rate even when interactions hold. They split results by format and look at saves, shares and comments, which matter more than likes now. They check cadence gaps and posting times from the account's own data and review the last 90 days of top posts for topic and hook patterns. The fix is usually a small set of repeatable content pillars, a written look and voice guide, a cadence the team can keep, and a calendar planned ahead, then two-week review loops that change one thing at a time.

steps.name: Find and organise the brand assets and write a short look and voice guide
steps.why: Staff cannot post consistently without a written look and voice.

steps.name: Pull six months of post and follower data
steps.why: The drop has to be seen post by post, by format and by week.

steps.name: Check the engagement-rate definition and the size of the drop
steps.why: Rates differ by denominator and actions counted; a target is only meaningful on the same measure.

steps.name: Diagnose cadence, format mix, timing, content and reply habits
steps.why: Each cause needs a different fix.

steps.name: Choose a few content pillars and a cadence the staff can keep
steps.why: Repeatable pillars and a fixed rhythm replace posting whenever there is time.

steps.name: Plan a calendar ahead with drafts, roles and approval
steps.why: A plan with an owner for each post makes the routine work across three staff.

steps.name: Schedule in Meta Business Suite and reply to comments
steps.why: Scheduling and replying are live actions that need approval.

steps.name: Review every two weeks and change one thing
steps.why: Short loops show what worked on the same measure.

pitfalls.text: Chasing a target rate on a different definition than the one reported.
Reading likes alone while saves, shares and comments move.
Posting in bursts with long gaps, which slows reach on the posts that follow.
Writing a brand guide no one uses because staff have no templates or schedule.
Changing format, timing and content all at once, so nothing can be learned.

stages.name: Pin down the goal, measure and limits
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured goal with one agreed definition of engagement rate, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Build the brand look and voice guide
stages.goal: Find the brand files in Drive, read the account's best posts, and write a one-page look and voice guide with colour pairs, logo use, photo style, caption voice and templates.

checks.name: Every colour, logo rule and voice rule traces to a Drive file or a post the owner approved
Missing items are listed as questions for the owner, not invented
Staff can follow it in one page, with an example good post and a not-this example
Colour pairs used for text are checked for readability

stages.name: Pull the post and follower history
stages.goal: Export six months of post results and the weekly follower chart into the project data folder and note exactly what was pulled.

checks.name: Covers six months before and after the drop began, or states what is missing
Post counts and follower totals match what Insights shows for the same dates
Format, poster and saves, shares and comments are present or their absence is noted

stages.name: Check the drop and the definition
stages.goal: Recompute engagement rate from the post data in both ways (by followers and by reach), compare with the reported 4% and 1.8%, and note how follower growth changed the rate.

checks.name: The rate is computed by followers and by reach, with the actions counted, and the owner picks the one the target uses
The reported fall from about 4% to 1.8% is reproduced or the difference explained
The effect of follower growth and non-follower Reels reach on the rate is shown
Published averages are shown only with their definition, and a 3.5% target is checked against them
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the target

stages.name: Find what changed
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the post data: cadence gaps, format mix, timing, content themes, replies and look consistency. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the posts and weeks behind it
Format and timing findings state how many posts each rests on; small groups are marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
Saves, shares and comments are read apart from likes

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into a short list of changes (pillars, formats, cadence, templates, reply routine), each with the finding it rests on, expected effect, staff effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect, staff hours a week, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
The total weekly staff time fits three people posting around shifts
States whether 3.5% on the agreed definition is likely, and what would have to be true

stages.name: Owner and cafe manager choose
stages.goal: The owner and cafe manager pick what to change and the posting rhythm. Ask why when a top option is passed over, and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options and the reasons are recorded
The posting rhythm is one the cafe manager agrees staff can keep

stages.name: Make the post templates and look checklist
stages.goal: Turn the brand guide into reusable carousel and Reel cover recipes, a caption pattern per pillar and a short look checklist for staff to run before posting.

checks.name: Every template uses the approved colours, logo rules and fonts
The checklist can be run in under two minutes by a staff member
Only files from the Drive folder are used; nothing is invented

stages.optional_when: No look or template change was chosen.

stages.name: Write the calendar, roles and drafts
stages.goal: Plan four weeks of posts by pillar, format and day, give each post an owner among the three staff, and draft captions and shot ideas from facts the cafes confirm.

checks.name: No offer, price, event or product claim appears unless the cafe confirmed it
Every post has a staff owner, a day and an approver
Captions pass the brand voice guide
The count of posts a week matches the chosen rhythm
Each post has alt text and a call for a save, share or comment that fits it

stages.name: Schedule posts after approval
stages.goal: Register what each batch should change, then with approval schedule the approved posts in Meta Business Suite and read the calendar back. Replies to comments are drafted and posted only when approved.

checks.name: Each batch is written down with its expected result before it is scheduled
Only posts the owner or cafe manager approved are scheduled
Date, time, format and caption in Business Suite match the approved draft
Each two-week batch changes one thing so the result can be read

stages.name: Read results every two weeks
stages.goal: Every two weeks read engagement on the agreed definition against 3.5%, by format, with saves, shares and comments, followers, posting count and the look check.

checks.name: Each readout uses the same definition and compares with the same earlier period
No format verdict from fewer than the planned number of posts; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Followers, posting count, look checklist pass rate and approved-only posting are checked
The gap to 3.5% is shown

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each two-week test, record what worked, propose rules with their scope, and plan the next quarter.

checks.name: Every test is closed with a verdict
Each rule says if it holds for this post, this account or all cafes

hypotheses.statement: Part of the drop is the measure: follower growth or Reels reaching non-followers lowered a rate that is calculated by followers.
hypotheses.test: Recompute by followers and by reach and compare with follower growth by week.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The rate by reach is steadier than the rate by followers.
hypotheses.refute_if: Both fall by a similar amount.

hypotheses.statement: Posting in bursts and gaps lowered reach on following posts.
hypotheses.test: Posts per week and the gaps between posts against reach per post.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Reach falls after gaps of two weeks or more.

hypotheses.statement: The format mix shifted toward images, which earn fewer saves and shares, and away from carousels and Reels.
hypotheses.test: Share of posts and median saves, shares and comments by format over time.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Image share rose and its saves and shares are lower.
hypotheses.refute_if: Mix is stable or images perform as well.

hypotheses.statement: Content drifted from what the audience saves and shares to generic or promotional posts.
hypotheses.test: Top 10 and bottom 10 posts of the last 90 days by saves and shares, by topic and hook.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Top posts share a theme the recent posts lack.
hypotheses.refute_if: Recent posts match the top themes.

hypotheses.statement: The messy look reduces recognition and engagement because posts do not read as one brand.
hypotheses.test: Rate the grid against the new guide and compare engagement of posts that match with those that do not.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Posts that match the look do better.

hypotheses.statement: Comments and messages go unanswered, which lowers reach and repeat engagement.
hypotheses.test: Share of comments and DMs answered within a day and engagement on posts after replies.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Replies are rare and engagement on posts with replies is higher.

measurement.window: Read every two weeks for three months; judge a format or pillar change after at least two review periods.
measurement.min_volume: No format or pillar verdict from fewer than 6 posts per group; always use the same engagement definition the owner chose.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause a change if followers fall, if a post carries a claim the cafes did not confirm, or if the look checklist is skipped; otherwise finish the two weeks before judging.
